description: Aerolineas Argentinas Aerolineas Plus miles for Aerolineas Argentinas flights. Miles = distance x a % set by the first letter of the fare basis (fare) and the zone: Domestic (both airports in Argentina), Regional (Argentina and Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay or Colombia) or International (Argentina and the US, Mexico, the Dominican Republic or Europe), from 0% to 200%, rounded down, no minimum and no elite bonus. A flight that does not touch Argentina, or a letter the zone does not list, is refused with a message. Progress toward Oro (25,000 qualifying miles or 30 segments), Platino (50,000 or 60) and Diamante (70,000 or 80) in 12 months; sm and fl are the miles and segments so far. Give segs: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and the ISO country codes of its two airports. Takes no price. Uses cwsi.net's calculator and the airline's published rules. Unofficial.

creditClass.description: The booking class letter on the ticket, for creditTo (required with creditTo). Ignored without creditTo.

creditFlights.description: The flights for creditTo: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and optionally from/to airport codes. Defaults to segs when they carry miles.

from.description: The departure airport's code; labels the breakdown.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's code; labels the breakdown.

creditStatus.description: Your status in the creditTo program, by its name as listed under creditTo. Defaults to the base level. Ignored without creditTo.

creditTo.description: Credit the flights to a partner program instead of Aerolineas Argentinas's own: flying-blue = Flying Blue (creditStatus one of: Explorer, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Ultimate). Earns by each flight's distance and the booking class at the program's published partner rates; leave creditTo out for the airline's own program. Give the booking class letter as creditClass. The flights are segs (their miles), or creditFlights.

fare.description: First letter of your fare basis. A = A (Domestic 0%, regional 25%, international 25%); B = B (Domestic 100%, regional 125%, international 125%); C = C (Domestic not listed, regional 150%, international 200%); D = D (Domestic not listed, regional 150%, international 200%); E = E (Domestic 25%, regional 25%, international 25%); G = G (Domestic 0%, regional 0%, international 0%); H = H (Domestic 75%, regional 100%, international 100%); I = I (Domestic not listed, regional 150%, international 200%); J = J (Domestic not listed, regional 150%, international 200%); K = K (Domestic 75%, regional 100%, international 100%); L = L (Domestic 75%, regional 100%, international 100%); M = M (Domestic 100%, regional 125%, international 125%); N = N (Domestic 25%, regional 25%, international 25%); Q = Q (Domestic 25%, regional 100%, international 100%); R = R (Domestic 0%, regional 25%, international 25%); S = S (Domestic 150%, regional 150%, international 150%); T = T (Domestic 25%, regional 25%, international 25%); U = U (Domestic 75%, regional 100%, international 100%); V = V (Domestic 25%, regional 25%, international 25%); W = W (Domestic 150%, regional 150%, international 150%); Y = Y (Domestic 100%, regional 125%, international 125%). Find the fare basis on your electronic ticket receipt: its first letter sets the percentage. Aerolineas does not map letters to cabins.

fl.description: Qualifying segments you have in the last 12 months (optional). Oro, Platino and Diamante can be reached with 30, 60 or 80 qualifying segments.

segs.description: The flights, one way and in order, one entry per flight (1 to 8): fromCountry and toCountry, the ISO 3166 two-letter country codes of its two airports; miles, its great-circle distance in miles (1 to 12,500); optional from and to, the IATA codes of its two airports, which label the breakdown; some airlines also use them (Vladivostok, VVO, on JAL and ANA; the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle, MAD-BCN, on Iberia; the long-haul tables named by city on SAS).

from.description: The departure airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

fromCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the departure airport, e.g. DE.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

toCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the arrival airport, e.g. DE.

sm.description: Qualifying miles you have in the last 12 months (optional). Miles earned by fare on Aerolineas Argentinas and SkyTeam flights, without status or promotion extras.

status.description: Your Aerolineas Plus status. CL = Clasico; OR = Oro; PL = Platino; DI = Diamante. Used to show your next tier. Oro, Platino and Diamante members may earn extra miles, but no percentage is published, so none is added.

trip.description: Trip. ow = One way; rt = Round trip. Round trip counts the same flights back the other way.
